posts.body:
With the conclusion of the I Love You, ____! Jam, I've taken the time to play through all of the submissions. I thought I'd offer some feedback on each entry here.
A few notes:
- I have all respect and appreciation for everyone's effort to create a complete work of whatever length under a time limit. Any critical comments I make are to offer areas that dev might be able to improve on in their future work or ongoing project. And maybe point out things they didn't realize were lacking, or that other people might view differently.
- I know some people don't want to read anything that isn't "Good job!" So, I give everybody who participated a "Good job for producing a contribution!" and all of your more specific and critical comments are in spoilers - if you don't want to see it, don't click it
If anyone's curious and reads through these and sees me repeating myself...sorry! I'm writing this under the assumption that each dev will only read their own section, so any repeated mistakes/notes are going to be repeated for each person they apply to.
Spoiler:
Rat World
@Crazetex
I’m not going to go too hard on this because it seems like just a throwaway to get a game in the jam for the badges, which is perfectly fair.
It appears to have no story, just random encounters on the map, and the troops are full of rats. The combat isn’t particularly fun, as the rats are HP sponges and only the characters with spells do decent damage to them (why do the other actors have Skill menus if they’re empty?).
So congrats on your participation. I didn’t see the credits required by the EULA for a distributed RPG Maker game. There doesn’t appear to be any win condition in the game to get to a credits screen, and there’s no text file in the directory.
Spoiler:
Reid’s Way Home from... the desert!?
@SGHarlekin
Again, seems like a simple filler just to get participation, which is fine. This does have some actual gameplay and instructions, and it’s not a JRPG – so for being quick and easy to get it done, it was pretty clever.
My comments would be:
1 – It’s not intuitive that the entire map/screen looks the same but you’re actually limited to the three center spaces. I don’t see why they couldn’t be lined with stones or even a different colored sand/quicksand/something so the player sees they won’t be able to go there.
2 – You could’ve used some eventing logic to make sure the girls didn’t show up in the same lane too many times in a row, or didn’t ignore a lane for too long. I passed entire levels without having to move.
3 – The name of the folder/zip doesn’t represent the name of the game.
4 – I didn’t see the credits required by the EULA for a distributed RPG Maker game. There doesn’t appear to be any win condition in the game to get to a credits screen, and there’s no text file in the directory.
Spoiler:
The 2026 "I Love You!" Banner
@TheAM-Dol
I downloaded the original version of this when you posted it, so I did not try the
Ensh/tified
version with no plugins. I thought it was a cute idea, the gacha sequence was well-made, and you had some good taste in names to use
I appreciated the satirical game update messages, but the loop went on for a bit long for me – stuff would cost more, but then I’d randomly get money from something, so it felt a bit dragging before I actually ran out of money and the game ended. I also couldn’t tell there was any actual point to the game, other than seeing the humorous messages. You told me after I played it that there’s a win condition of getting the max star drop of the character you selected on the screen.
Cute idea with some clever execution. I saw some credits at the end, but I don’t think they were correctly worded according to MV’s EULA.
Spoiler:
Baron von Piledriver's Puzzle Jam
@WaywardMartian
I liked this. The story and dialogue was cute and the puzzles show varied gameplay. I didn’t beat it, but I think it’s nice overall.
The ball-pushing puzzle was solidly designed. The solution wasn’t immediately obvious in the first level, but it only took me three tries to get the extra item and the exit.
In the first puzzle room, it seems buggy that you can push the balls against a wall and they still make the sliding sound (and it’ll spam if you hold the button down). You could’ve used some event logic to only play the sound if it moves.
In the second room, I think it would be a better UX decision to have a default choice when giving Peter the weeds or not – having the cursor start unselected and needing to press something to get onto the choices is a bit unintuitive. Also, “wanna” is slang for “want to” not “want a”.
I didn’t get past the second puzzle – I didn’t understand from the explanation which tiles were considered “fancy” and I died after trying to get onto the bottom row from three completely different-looking tiles and getting zapped on each. I’m not sure what the rationale was to not allow saves or replaying that room, but I wasn’t going to replay the first puzzle and all the conversations just to try it again.
As a side note – the Dropbox account you’re hosting the download from appears to have your full real name on it. I don’t know if that’s something you intended to be public.
Spoiler:
Reid’s Secret Date
@Welleran
Right off the bat, the music is quite loud. Aside from that, there’s a great overuse of exclamation marks. If your character is exclaiming or shouting everything, it loses any contextual meaning of emphasis. Use periods unless something is actually supposed to stick out.
Exploring the bedroom, I appreciate the descriptions for various items; there are some minor English errors, mostly with randomly capitalized words which shouldn’t be, and with “You got
the a
Chocolate box” and “now work” instead of “no work”. But as you’re not working in your native language, the English is fine and understandable.
I got past the first corridor in two tries, but I nearly gave up on the second room. I know the hint says “maybe the crates,” but I just figured that meant being next to a crate would block line of sight (it doesn’t). It’s completely unintuitive that you can simply walk through the crates in all directions, and I only figured it out by accident on my last try when I held a button down too long.
I have no idea what the dialogue with the dog on the third screen is about...if it’s supposed to be funny or a reference to something, it was lost on me. When meeting Kasey, again the music is horribly loud. There are also some wrong words in the dialogue, but nothing huge.
The ending seemed like there was something broken in your event logic. My date was interrupted by the dog attacking me, and the end-game text said Roza was angry that Reid had set the dog on her, but nothing like that had ever happened...so it made no sense.
I think the idea of a stealth game to sneak off on a date is cute, and the mapping is actually pretty good. It also shows some decent use of eventing, to change the movement speed on different tiles and kick the barrels and such. But the unintuitive puzzles and erroneous logic detracted from the final product.
Your game does not appear to contain the credits required by RPG Maker’s EULA.
Spoiler:
Beast Hunters
@Axius
I couldn’t try anything, the itch link provided had no content.
Spoiler:
I Can’t Reid
@Willibab
I see you’re not using VisuStella plugins – have you modified your NW.js? I haven’t seen this text glitch in vanilla MZ projects.
Why on earth is every word in your dialogue capitalized? It’s really jarring to read.
Then I had a conversation with the shopkeeper and it was just weird to read. There are also sundry other errors – “I’m” should have an apostrophe (it appeared to be wrong every single time I saw it), “the God’s” should not. For a game that’s primarily driven by its text, all of this is quite off-putting and I had to force myself to keep playing and give the game its fair share of time.
I wish you didn’t manually control all of the timing on so many of the Show Texts. I prefer to be able to speed up the display since I read quickly.
The southern gate doesn’t allow me to pass even though there’s nothing visibly obstructing it and there’s no evented reason (like her saying to herself “I bet my daughter is still in town”).
The mapping I think is nice, although the event to the main character’s house appears to be accidentally left on Action Button instead of Player Touch.
Then the final scene with the scrolling text for the letter is written using proper English, although about half of the time your line breaks are too early and there’s empty space remaining to the right. Also, “cheerish” your loved ones was misspelled (which I note just because it’s conspicuous, being the moral of your story).
I appreciate you included the correct credits, and the maps seemed well-made. I also appreciate the notion of exploring a war-torn village and interpreting the love theme with a lost love; but I can’t say I enjoyed reading the story. I want to give you a break as English is not your native language, but in your forum posts you clearly demonstrate that you know the correct way to use capitalization in English, so I just have no idea what you were going for here.
Spoiler:
That Time I Saved You
@rafaeljbi
First impression: the zipped archive is called GAME_JAM_EN_US_windows and the folder inside is just Game_Jam. Your distribution should reflect the actual name of your game.
Second impression: the opening shot is nice. The moving bars on the top and bottom of the screen and the movement of the text while the actors walk down the street is very slick. It doesn’t seem like you adjusted the sound, though – the default volume for RPG Maker games is very loud, and you should always turn it down. When you’re able to use plugins, I have a Dev Volume plugin for that, but you can do it manually by lowering the volume on all the tracks you use in the editor, or by lowering the volume in the playtest before deploying your project.
Some of the text goes past the width of the message window and gets cut off.
Other places, you line break way too early and there’s empty space in the window.
The eventing on the mine cart puzzle was well-done – I just wish that Reid dying didn’t go so far back and replay all the opening messages and instructions every time. Just reset the puzzle...clicking through those extra windows took me as much time as doing the puzzle until I figured out the correct path.
I think the jumping puzzle has a bit of an inherent flaw in that the button on the bottom of the area isn’t visible from the top – so you have no choice but to start jumping and decide your path before you have any idea where you’re supposed to end up.
Also, the directions seem misleading. They talk about moving 4 tiles and 2 tiles – which is correct from a mapping perspective – but when the only spaces you can go on are the pillars, it seemed intuitive that you were saying I would jump 4 or 2
pillars
, not counting the water spaces that were irrelevant. Maybe that’s just me.
It’s also not fun that you can get stuck – if you end up in the upper-right corner, these two arrows will bounce you back and forth forever. And since there’s no reset button/item/command, if that happens you have to just sit there until the time eventually runs out so you can try again.
The same is true of the second column on the left side. This one’s even worse, because literally your first step here locks you into an endless loop and you have to wait for the entire timer.
This second room is where I gave up. I think the concept of the puzzle is fine, but not being able to see the entire thing to plan my path, and having so little ability to adjust if you don’t make the right choice immediately, just made it frustrating.
I really enjoyed the concept of this one, I liked the dialogue between Reid and Priscilla, and the gameplay of going through their past puzzles as they bickered with each other is clever. I just didn’t like it enough to brute force my way through that second room.
Spoiler:
Kitty’s Day
@Midona018
I think the premise of the game and the maps are fine. It would be nice to have some direction – giving me some idea where Granny is, rather than making me just run around talking to every NPC and checking every door until I find her.
It’s weird to have a space between the end of a word and an exclamation mark or question mark. I’m happy to go easy on some of the odd word choices and such since you’re not a native speaker, but I’ve never seen French writing put an extra space before those marks and you don’t do it before periods...so I dunno why you have that everywhere.
There’s a bug when you’re ordering food in the restaurant. You have to stand next to the menu to activate the event, but it immediately teleports you a space down into the chair. Then the choice menu comes up and you don’t have a default option set, so the player needs to press a key just to bring the cursor into view.
Speaking of the restaurant...that whole portion seems to be bugged. When you walk in, Kitty says it would be easier to order take out than to look for all her ingredients to cook dinner. But after I get take out, I bring it home and the counter in my house still says I need to find all the ingredients for the meal! That’s where I lost patience and gave up.
I agree with you that Kitty is cute; the premise of a little fetch quest to make a simple jam game is fine, and your mapping also looks decent to me. But the eventing errors and lack of any kind of guidance just put me off – I felt like I was just running around talking to everyone until I did the right thing by accident, and then it still might not work.
Spoiler:
Magical Girl Priscilla: Funny Farm
@KV_Kingdom
This is cute. The very first screen is a little eye-shocking with how much of the screen is the bright grass and flowers – but I think the crew doing a magical girl transformation into their adventurer forms is cute.
And the actual gameplay of quizzing the animals is also cute, several of the responses made me laugh. I noticed one typo “an acutal fairy” – but otherwise, all the dialogue was solid and clever.
I do think it would’ve been nice for some of the choices to actually be animals; it seems to make keeping score less relevant if you should always just choose the same answer.
I appreciate you had the correct credits at the end, and I thought it was a solid, cute game.
Spoiler:
2k3MZ
@orochii
I almost gave this one a pass because it had no download option – I’m not a fan of running software out of my browser. But I figured that wouldn’t be fair, so here I go! And don’t take it personally, I know some people are the opposite and will only play Web versions.
The sound effects are really loud. They need to be brought down from the default volume level in the editor, or by lowering volume in the options before deploying.
You have a UX issue which is present throughout the game: your line breaks are way too early, leaving large gaps on the right side of message windows. It looks weird and lopsided.
I did chuckle at the smuggling bananas job.
A lot of the other stuff I think was supposed to be funny fell flat (at least for me) – the meta-jokes talking about game variables, players not wanting to read storyline, the developer wants to tell me something. Being funny is probably the hardest kind of game to try to make, so going at it heavily will almost always be a miss for some chunk of people – and meta humor is one of the most challenging to make actually funny. Again, for my tastes.
There are a few typos – something about the residents giving “your” their patronage, the bunny dancer talks about “paragidms,” but overall the writing is fine. All of my conversations in the town were fruitless, then I got to this one in the Inn and I was just done.
I think your use of incorporating the old assets into MZ is a neat choice, and some parts of the game’s premise were funny, but too many of them just weren’t.
Spoiler:
For the Love of RPG Maker
@unity
I think the writing is cute, and the mashing of the various RTPs is appropriate. You have some bits of dialogue where the line breaks are premature, leaving empty space to the right of the window.
The wording when you open chests – “item name GET” – is off-puttingly weird. I don’t know if it’s intentionally emulating something that I’m not familiar with, so obviously if that’s the case, cool. But otherwise...odd.
There’s a lot of stuff in the store for a game that’s supposed to be over in 30 minutes, and has taken about 5 to get to the shop in the first place.
Again, I don’t know if it’s just using a default name from another RTP, but “little kobold” would be correctly contracted to “li’l,” not “lil’”.
As I went through the maps, the various little conversations took up time, and several of the enemies are rather HP-sponge-y, which made the fights take a bit longer than they might have. I ended up running around, avoiding fights and conversations, just looking for the memories to see if I could finish the game within the 30-minute time limit. I ended up finding two of them, and stopped after that.
I appreciate the premise of the game, making a retrospective of the games you’ve designed and revisiting characters from them. I also give you props for the number of maps you made and the resizing of the graphics to fit into the engine. The writing was also overall good. But between the number of maps, the fights, the full-blown equipment system and all the shops and stuff, I think the scope crept substantially past what was expected for this jam. For the amount I saw, nice work.
Spoiler:
Dungeon Mark
@bandwidthslayer
I didn’t try this game because it was flagged as quarantined for “suspicious behavior” by itch. I didn’t get that from other people whose game was just the executable, so I didn’t think it was worth taking chances.
Spoiler:
Hope’s Cure
@StarWolff
First impression: the opening theme is painfully loud. The default volume in RPG Maker is too loud, you need to either turn down the volume on the tracks in the editor or lower it in the options before deployment.
This text is cut off on the right side. This is just the first time, there are several places in the game where it happens.
There are some issues with this mapping style.
When you have the top ceiling tiles against the top of the map in the editor, it automatically draws them as if they were continuing up off the screen. You can correct this with shift-click mapping, but typically one just allows an extra, empty tile on all sides so it shows the finished ceiling.
Then, the way you show the top and side ceilings but nothing along the bottom just looks odd, especially the two places on the right as it bumps up and you see just one and two tiles of ceiling. It also makes it weirder for you to show where a door/passage is, as there’s additional wall/ceiling missing there.
The Dark Forest map seems overly large – and why would someone cut/walk the path around that large loop instead of simply cutting south through the huge gap between the trees?
Why don’t the skills have descriptions? They have them by default, so you had to intentionally remove them; now there’s an empty window in your UI and I don’t know why Fire and Spark don’t cost the same amount of MP.
The Castle Grounds map is weird, to just appear in the middle of an island with no apparent entrance/path that you got there from. Again, though, it’s really overly large and doesn’t have a lot of visual details to be interesting.
There are some minor typos, but I can forgive those with English not being your first language; the writing has some incorrect sentence structure, but is understandable. When you’re working on a full project that you’d release for people to play, definitely look into getting an editor and using grammar tools like in Microsoft Word or Google Docs. In the skill messages, the damage is correct (takes X damage) but the healing is backwards (heals HP X). I know that’s how it comes by default, but it’s easy to notice and correct in the Terms tab.
The combat overall isn’t particularly interesting, as Marsha only has the option of hitting one enemy, hitting them all, or saving MP; Cat has no option other than does someone need to be healed or not; and Horse has no skill options at all.
The Dog battle particularly was boring, as he has a lot of HP and all of your party members are going to just choose the same options every single turn. Then the battle against the mage is one of my pet peeves in games – if there’s an unwinnable fight, don’t waste my time trying to do the fight. Just make the story say they fail in their attack and keep going.
At the end, your game is lacking the credits that are legally required by the EULA of RPG Maker, and I don’t see them in a text file in the game folder. You want to make sure you pay attention to things like that, as it would be disheartening to release a full game at some point just to get into legal trouble.
Overall, the game itself had a cute premise and worked fine, but you want to work a bit on your mapping and combat.
Spoiler:
Everybody Loves Blanchette
@Lady_JJ
Lol, Farmer Bovine? There was a weird bug in the first scene where Blanchette went to leave but the cat was in her way, so it took almost ten seconds of waiting for the cat to move so she could move another space, inching her way to the door.
On the second screen, I don’t think the dark blue text with no window background against the green grass is a good choice – it’s pretty hard to read, and where the letters get on top of the trees, it’s all but illegible.
Then the rest of that village map is surprisingly huge and empty. Like, there’s the whole screen with nothing but the edges of some houses. That’s visually uninteresting and it makes the player feel like they’re wasting their time just walking through space.
The opening of the game isn’t bad, but some of the other music is quite loud. The BGMs don’t sound like they’re at a uniform level.
The picture puzzle is a neat idea, but I wish it told me what to do beyond saying I could use Escape to quit. I wasted several moves before I figured out what was happening when I pressed things.
If you tell the farmer you quit, leave the house and come back, there’s a graphical bug where the three events spawn in one position then teleport a space after the screen fades in.
The game has style, between the colored text, the little informational pop ups, and the sound effects. The writing is also good, aside from a few minor typos. (quick aside – “-ly” words are, as a rule, adverbs. They modify how the verb is being done. So when you say someone “smells badly” or “smells horribly,” that means they are bad at smelling things with their nose. Saying they “smell bad” or “smell horrible” is using adjectives to describe their odor)
I also note you using the appropriate credits at the end. I think the notion of a slice of life story featuring your favorite character is appropriate for the jam, the writing is good, and you have some clever eventing in there. But your village map and some of the text colors and placement with no background needs some time to playtest.
Spoiler:
I love you my little fanatic
@PoopsyTheDuck
Okay...this was a bit of a rough one. I know you’ve just picked up the software recently and this is your first effort, so I’m going to make sure to include advice on that. But at the same time, a lot of the issues here feel like low effort or not putting thought into the work, and I’m going to be straight with you about that, too.
Disclaimer – I don’t usually try to open other people’s games as projects, as I think it’s disrespectful. But in this case, I had to, because your initial upload wasn’t a correctly deployed game. So aside from what I experienced while playing, I saw some stuff about how you made it in the editor.
So, first bit of advice: the way you draw your maps is off.
You’re using only walls here, no ceilings. You can see how it looks weird and cut off on the bottom, going directly from wall to the floor. I’m also not sure how you managed to make the autotiles do a few of the things they’re doing, but you should be able to see right away how there are partial pillars getting cut off as they run into the wall. Lastly, you’re using an inconsistent height for the walls. They’re two tiles high on the bottom edge but only one tile high on the top, which gives the whole thing a vaguely Escher-like look.
Aside from that, the English right off the bat is very poor. I would cut you some slack if it wasn’t your native language, but your profile says English has been your first language for 23 years, so it’s a very reasonable assumption that you should know when to properly capitalize words, not have so many spelling errors, and be able to use the correct words and conjugations of words.
Just this one shot has four significant errors, and it’s pretty typical of the writing in the game as a whole.
When you’re playing a game that is primarily story conveyed through text, this is what comes across as being low effort and apparently making no effort to make that text correct at a basic level.
To get back into editor/development tips, again note the above screenshot – you see how you made a line break after the (wrong) word “change” and there’s so much empty space to the right? That doesn’t look good. You should keep a sentence going all the way across the message window until the next word won’t fit, just like the way text is printed in books.
Gameplay-wise, the game is frustrating immediately off the bat. The only way to make it progress is to do what you’re told
not
to do (make noise), then doing the reasonable thing of escaping while the girl isn’t looking somehow magically pushes you backward with a closed door and just spontaneously gives you a game over. It wasn’t until my fourth try that out of sheer lack of any other ideas, I tried interacting with the guard I’m supposed to be avoiding, which leads to the nonsense above and actually lets me go to the next screen.
The infinite hallway, again, has mapping issues with weirdly-formatted autotiles. It’s also very annoying to have him popping up with dialogue about how weird the hallway is every two steps. Luckily, I saw and stepped on the pebbles tile or I’m sure I would’ve gotten another game over.
In the cave area, I pretty much avoided everything and tried to just find a way through, but I will offer some more mapping feedback.
You have walls one tile high but you’ve put cracks that are two tiles tall on them, so it looks like the cracks are somehow bending up over the ceiling. From a gameplay perspective, the player sees doorway-sized cracks like that and expects them to do
something
. Even if they’re not exits to another area, I’d expect a message about being able to see something (why is there light shining through one if it doesn’t go outside?). But them just being there and not doing anything when you walk into them is weird.
I got outside of the cave, which for some reason is right next to my house. I walked in, my character says it smells bad, and...I got a Game Over. At that point, I certainly wasn’t going to argue with replaying anything, so I took that as good enough.
As I mentioned, I did poke at a few other things while I had the project open in the editor. Here’s something I wanted to point out:
This is done incorrectly in several ways. First, the Set Weather Effect sets the weather effect. It should only be done once. That means putting it inside a Loop is wrong, you do not want to be constantly resetting the weather 60 times a second.
Additionally, Parallel and Autorun event triggers
already
loop. That means you shouldn’t be putting a Loop inside of one. It also means it’s incorrect to not be turning the event off – again, you don’t want to be constantly running the weather command.
Then, just take an objective look at this:
All of those events cause a game over if you touch them. Your game doesn’t allow the player to save. So a person would have to constantly replay the entire thing to get to this hallway again and again to figure out the specific one-tile path they’re supposed to take to reach the guy at the end.
Do you really think anyone is going to do that? Do you really think anyone would think doing that is fun?
Ultimately, I really don’t know what you were trying to do with this game. I think the concept of focusing on a bit member of the RTP cast is cute, but everything from the writing throughout the game to the actual gameplay feels like you put no thought into what someone else playing your game would think.
Hopefully, some of the editor tips above will help you use the software better, but it really seems like you need to do the tutorials included in MV. There are other issues I didn’t go through, like not turning off events that shouldn’t be accessible again, turning on switches that are never referenced, stuff that’s very basic MV usage. Good luck with your future projects.
Spoiler:
The Healer’s Trial
@Crim_T
First impression: I’m not sure what you did to produce this. There are lots of files missing, as if you deployed the game with the “exclude unused files” option checked. But then there’s a project file sitting there for anyone to open the project with, which wouldn’t be there from a deployment. There’s also an autosave sitting in there. So it has an initially weird presentation.
This isn’t anything horrible, but to my tastes the dialogue reads a bit oddly sometimes. The way you have extra spaces between line breaks makes the text look sort of splayed out. There’s also some random capitalization. I can kind of understand it when it’s a quest keyword (although I would argue it’s not necessary to both give the word a different color and capitalize it), but why would there be “dark Rye bread”? Similarly, “Thank ya kindly, Your rooms..” Also, is there a reason that the colored keywords are different colors? It gives some messages a kind of unicorn-vomit vibe.
There are also some places where you’re missing periods. It’s not like it’s every sentence, but it’s more than a one-off error.
Last in terms of dialogue, I’d draw your attention to this. A lot of your line breaks are put in far before the actual end of the line, leaving lots of blank space on the right side of the window. It’s visually obtrusive to have that empty space – I think it would be better to reduce your UI size or type to the end of the lines.
Like here, almost half the screen is empty.
In the first map, I like the conversing NPCs and the dancer’s routine on the stage. The music does seem a bit out of place to have this techno-y track in a medieval fantasy setting.
Moving forward, the instructions aren’t correct for the charging minigame. It says “press the directional keys as prompted in relation to the main character” which would mean if the character is facing right on the screen and it tells me left, I would press up because that’s left in relation to the main character. But in fact, it actually wants me to press left when the flame appears to the left on the screen, even though that’s the character’s right. Also, I think the timing is too tight – it took me a lot of tries to succeed in the game. But I do appreciate that you offer the automatic pass after a few failures.
I only know the next bit because I looked at the hint book...I would never have guessed to do all the stuff in the bar from any kind of hints/information actually in the game. I was on the verge of leaving the village and taking the game over. At least make the old man say he saw the escort talking to the bartender or helping behind the bar, or give
some
clue that I’m supposed to be doing stuff on this map.
Channel’s skill text has a typo, it says “restored MP X” rather than “restored X MP”. I know that’s how it comes by default, but it’s easy to notice and correct in the Terms tab.
I finished up my play after beating the bartender. I poked around the town a bit and realized I had no idea what else to do without reading through your hint book, so I was done there.
I think your story was good and the writing was decent. Mapping was fine for my tastes, and you definitely did some respectable stuff with eventing. But I think you need to put a bit more thought into how players will know what to do. Just having no prompts/guidance of any kind and relying on people randomly clicking on literally everything (why, logically, would I think to go into the item shop and inspect the bookshelf in the corner?) isn’t something that most players are going to do.
Spoiler:
Rise of the Farmer
@Reim_Harbert
The music volume is a bit loud – the default volume in the engine is too loud. You need to make sure you turn down the volume in the tracks you use, or turn down the volume in the in-game options menu before you deploy.
The first few maps are fine – the horse blocking the way is cute. It’s also a cute twist to have the farmer come in and take out the heroes for robbing his house.

With the conclusion of the I Love You, ____! Jam, I've taken the time to play through all of the submissions. I thought I'd offer some feedback on each entry here.
A few notes:
- I have all respect and appreciation for everyone's effort to create a complete work of whatever length under a time limit. Any critical comments I make are to offer areas that dev might be able to improve on in their future work or ongoing project. And maybe point out things they didn't realize were lacking, or that other people might view differently.
- I know some people don't want to read anything that isn't "Good job!" So, I give everybody who participated a "Good job for producing a contribution!" and all of your more specific and critical comments are in spoilers - if you don't want to see it, don't click it
If anyone's curious and reads through these and sees me repeating myself...sorry! I'm writing this under the assumption that each dev will only read their own section, so any repeated mistakes/notes are going to be repeated for each person they apply to.

The primary factor to all of this is going to be context (which I think I explained in my original write-up, but I'm happy to put forth again). The fact that I do not know these characters, don't know the things they've done together, don't know what they've said to each other before, so I have no context, was a very large part of why it felt boring.
Some of these conversations might have been perfectly fine in the middle of a larger game, where I have come to know these characters and I understand the other things they're referencing. Without that, it's like sitting there listening to two other people talk about the stuff they did while they were hanging out the other day.
Then some of the rest of it is how things are said. Just trading sentences back and forth gets generally dull. I recall a fanboy soldier I talked to who was excited to meet me - he was overexcited, I was a bit nonplussed at his enthusiasm, that dialogue was interesting because it showed me two different personalities.
Me talking to a soldier who basically says "Hi. I'm building this." is not interesting, because it literally conveys nothing of interest.
I quit in the middle of the meeting with Ilia because of the accumulation - it wasn't that I recall her conversation being
worse
than other parts of the game, but I had come to understand that I wasn't going to find any of it interesting and I felt I'd played long enough to give a fair amount of feedback.

Click to expand...
Not a renowned general engaging in menial tasks. I acknowledge that's a very JRPG thing to do, so maybe that's your intent and your target audience is people who like that part of Japanese games - like being the leader of the rebellion's army in Suikoden and you're gathering bath salts for someone, or a professor and general in Fire Emblem: Three Houses and you're going shopping for candy.
Again, there's the issue of context - I didn't witness or actually help in the battle to take this city, I didn't level up this character, I have no connection to anything that's happening. But, generally speaking, talking to someone who's organizing the triage facility or doing something to decide how the limited incoming supplies are allocated or restructuring the troop composition of our depleted formations...those seem like they'd be interesting situations that are appropriate for the character.
Or, since it's supposed to be his day off, actually doing day off things. Does he work out? Find soldiers to spar with? Have some kind of hobby he finds a way to participate in?
Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous has some good events/decisions for a general in charge of an army.
ValentinaSama67 said:
About this, that is actually the intention, you're supposed to be thrown into Vice's life with not a lot of prior knowledge...Considering this is what I was trying to achieve with the story and characters, what would you recommend I do, to make it a more interesting experience and to instigate in the player, curiosity to find out more?
Click to expand...
I don't know that you can. Yes, every RPG has you thrown into someone's life with no prior knowledge. But at least you're
beginning
their story, you're there as they start doing the stuff they're doing, as they meet the people they're going to interact with.
To me, the concept of just being thrown into the middle of a story entirely doesn't make me at all curious to sit through conversations referring to prior events and I slowly piece together the beginning of the story. You probably will find some people who would want to do that, there are people for every taste.
For something that's intentionally of limited scope like a jam game, I just don't think it's a great concept to have something that's alluding to a larger story.
I will say that having more personality in different characters will help keep your dialogue from feeling monotonous - try to give them different speech patterns, different emotional reactions, etc.
That's really all I think I can recall...I played a lot of different games, and at this point I played them, like, a week ago. So I think all of that stuff is relevant to your game, and I wish you luck with your project.
